title: Low-Rim Confidence Shooting
description: Young or new players shoot at a lowered portable rim with a smaller ball, so they can use correct form and see the ball go in — a key PE and mini-basketball adaptation.

content.objective: Build correct one-hand shooting form and confidence at a rim and ball size suited to the players' strength.
content.setup: Portable rims lowered to around 2.6 m (or as low as available) and size 5 balls; stations around the gym.
content.organization: Groups of three to four per rim; rotate stations every three minutes.
instructions: Stand close to the rim with feet shoulder-width and the ball on the fingertips.
Shoot with one hand, the other hand at the side.
Follow through: 'reach into the cookie jar' finish.
Score a point for every make; step back after three makes.
Rotate to the next rim on the whistle.
coachingPoints: Ball on the fingers, not the palm.
Bend the knees: the legs help the shot.
commonMistakes: Two-hand chest throws because the rim is too high.
Looking at the ball, not the rim.
content.safety: Portable rims weighted and stable; no hanging on rims; players wait their turn behind a line.
progressions: Raise the rim gradually as form holds.
Add a jump stop before the shot.
variations: Bank shots off the portable board.
successCriteria: Correct one-hand form on most shots.
content.gameApplication: Players who learn correct form early, at the right height, do not have to unlearn a chest throw later.
